strings.votre_projet_oss_est:
Your OSS project is used by thousands!
And earns you almost nothing?
strings.l_ia_commoditise_vos:
AI is commoditizing your advantages.
Hyperscalers fork your code.
Sovereignty budgets exist — but they don’t reach you.
Optimize your model!
strings.cinq_tensions_que_toute: Five tensions every OSS company runs into. Naming them is the first step.
strings.adoption_et_revenus_sont: Adoption and revenue are two distinct metrics. Most OSS companies optimize one and are surprised the other doesn’t follow.
strings.chaque_demande_d_un: Every power-user request is a distraction from what your ICP will pay for. Serve both without a model, and you lose both.
strings.sans_modele_clair_vous: Without a clear model, you lose both.
strings.les_services_professionnels_comblent: Professional services fill the revenue gap — until they consume your product team. 40% margin, 0% scalability.
strings.tracez_la_ligne_trop: Draw the line too early and the community forks you. Too late and enterprises have no reason to pay. That line is a product decision, not a legal one.
strings.la_frontiere_est_une: The boundary is a product decision.
strings.aws_et_azure_prennent: AWS and Azure take your Apache code, wrap it in managed hosting, and take your enterprise customers. You need defensibility before growth.
strings.les_poids_ouverts_et: Open weights and open data fuel a virtuous cycle: every use improves the model, every improvement attracts new contributors and customers. Used as an accelerator, open source AI multiplies your competitive advantage instead of eroding it.
strings.toute_entreprise_oss_ne: Not every OSS company should be a SaaS.
strings.le_bon_modele_depend: The right model depends on your code, your community and your customers — not on what’s trendy.
strings.ce_qui_reste_gratuit: What stays free, what becomes paid, and how to draw the line without forking your community or blocking your enterprise customers.
strings.quand_l_hebergement_ajoute: When hosting adds real value vs. when it’s ops theater. What makes your managed offering defensible against hyperscalers.
strings.comment_capter_les_revenus: How to capture professional services revenue without building a services company. Scope, margins and getting out of the trap.
strings.secteur_public_europeen_conformite: European public sector, sovereignty compliance, procurement cycles. The market is real — but it requires a different go-to-market.
strings.un_seul_modele_couvre: A single model rarely covers the whole field. Combine open-core and managed cloud, support and enterprise licensing — deliberately layering models builds resilience your competitors will struggle to replicate.
strings.divisez_votre_produit_en: Break your product into independent building blocks to target distinct segments, or bundle complementary offerings into coherent packages. The granularity of your catalog is itself a strategic variable.
strings.du_composant_unitaire_au: From single component to business package, from standalone tool to a platform that creates network effects among your customers. Building a scalable portfolio means recognizing that value doesn’t always lie in the code alone.
strings.placez_le_client_payant: Put the paying customer at the center of every product decision — not the technology, not the community, not the competition. Experiment deliberately: new models, new segments, new offerings. The most controlled disruption is the one you start yourself, at your own pace, before the market forces it on you.
strings.identifier_les_leviers_c: Identifying the levers is already the start of building.
strings.une_lecture_honnete_de: An honest reading of your situation — areas of opportunity, potential leaks, the first foundations of a sustainable model. Not a catalog of failures: a map of the first levers to pull.
strings.la_tranche_gratuite_absorbe: The free tier absorbs all usage — no structured upgrade path
strings.portes_de_valeur_claires: Clear value gates, structured freemium→paid conversion
strings.messaging_ecrit_pour_les: Messaging written for contributors, not buyers
strings.proposition_de_valeur_icp: ICP-specific value proposition, ready for decision-makers
strings.roadmap_pilotee_par_les: Roadmap driven by the loudest GitHub issues
strings.roadmap_pilotee_par_l: Roadmap driven by ICP revenue impact
strings.fonctionnalites_peu_utilisees_maintenues: Little-used features maintained at high cost, untapped telemetry, technical debt hiding real usage
strings.perimetre_allege_sur_les: Scope trimmed to real usage, telemetry put to work, lower maintenance costs
strings.ciblage_icp_imprecis_distribution: Vague ICP targeting, distribution limited to existing channels, lost deals left unanalyzed
strings.segments_a_fort_potentiel: High-potential segments activated, structured partner network, lessons from lost deals put to use
strings.depot_sans_signaux_de: Repository without trust signals, under-optimized SEO/GEO, untargeted event presence
strings.depot_structure_pour_la: Repository structured for conversion, optimized SEO/GEO, ICP-focused event presence
strings.presence_concentree_dans_la: Presence concentrated in the OSS community — within and across projects — little reach toward non-open-source audiences
strings.rayonnement_elargi_vers_des: Broader reach toward audiences beyond OSS: enterprises, integrators, public sector, industry influencers
strings.un_chemin_clair_etape: A clear path, step by step.
strings.pas_de_retro_planning: No 18-month backward planning. Three key phases, concrete deliverables, and a model you can execute as soon as we’re done.
strings.un_regard_honnete_sur: An honest look at your current situation — model, positioning, revenue, untapped levers.
strings.un_plan_d_action: An action plan prioritized by revenue impact — not by technical convenience or community noise.
strings.un_accompagnement_ancre_dans: Hands-on support grounded in real-world conditions — adjusted at each iteration, measured on the right indicators.
strings.prenons_30_minutes_pour: Let’s take 30 minutes to look at your situation together.
strings.pas_de_pitch_pas: No pitch. No slide deck. A candid conversation — you tell me where you stand, I tell you what I see.
strings.votre_produit_oss_tourne: Your OSS product works, your community is growing, but revenue isn’t keeping up yet.
strings.quelque_chose_coince_pricing: Something is stuck — pricing, positioning, roadmap — and you want an honest outside perspective.
strings.pas_besoin_d_un: No defined project needed. If the topic speaks to you, the conversation already has value.
